correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=3 and all real 0<t<2pi/n, h>0, the 2n listed lateral triangular support planes are reconstructed directly from vertices. At an upper vertex three planes and the cap yield exactly four strict inequalities. For even n antipodal planar normals bound upper illumination by n/2; for odd n cancellation produces an n-cycle of forbidden index pairs with independence floor(n/2). The explicit block vector has strict margins U<w<C from the two elementary inequalities 2L+t<pi and 2L+theta-t<pi. Cyclic blocks give both ordinary and fractional matching covers; lower layer follows by vertical reflection and angular relabeling. At aligned twist the planar polygon capacity is floor((n-1)/2). The independent standard-library checker directly replays 180 parameter triples, checking 6,660 facet incidence planes and every constructed coverage direction; finite checks are supporting evidence, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact ordinary and fractional profiles across a natural continuous shape parameter reveal a sharp discontinuity at the aligned prism for every even n, despite arbitrarily small geometric perturbations. The full classification in all n and h is motivated by the new universal fractional bound and by previously studied uniform antiprisms. The odd-cycle obstruction and constructive open-angle uniformity are reusable facet-incidence mechanisms; the result is not an arbitrary one-off numerical invariant.
